data.name: Jyotsvika
data.long_meaning: Jyotsvika is a Sanskrit name derived from the words ‘Jyot’ meaning light and ‘Svika’ meaning prosperity. This name is often given to girls to represent the Goddess of Light and Prosperity. In Hindu mythology, Jyotsvika is believed to bring good fortune, wisdom, and prosperity to those who bear this name.

historical_references.reference: Jyotsvika was a queen of the Vakataka dynasty in the 5th century CE. She is best known for her role as a patron of art and architecture during the reign of her husband, Pravarasena II.
historical_references.context: Vakataka Dynasty, Patronage of Art and Architecture

historical_references.reference: Jyotsvika is also mentioned in the Hindu epic, the Mahabharata, as the name of a celestial nymph, or apsara. In this context, she is described as the wife of the god Indra and the mother of the rain god, Varuna.
